svg.title: TOPAK A1 — The letters name roles, not products
svg.desc: Each letter of TOPAK carries an obligation. Any instrument that meets the obligation may be substituted for the reference's choice; the floor tier cannot change language without ADR-0030.
svg.text: TOPAK · A1

text.tspan: The letters name roles, not products

svg.text: Each letter of TOPAK carries an obligation. Any instrument that meets the obligation may be substituted for the reference's choice; the floor tier cannot change language without ADR-0030.

An agent is Byzantine at every deployment position. Safety cannot depend on what a model means or intends, so models stay out of the trusted computing base and every guarantee is stated against an agent that may do anything its alphabet allows (ADR-0007).
Specify every guarantee against what an agent's alphabet
allows, and check it, with a mutation that must fail for every
property.
TLA+: TLC over the tracked tools/tla2tools.jar
checks every mutation and witness. The TLA+ Proof
System (tlapm, T-0045-31) proves the invariants of
twenty-two modules, 5,225 obligations, every one
proved (ADR-0046; G10 §2.9). Nineteen certify: every
SMT obligation closed by a proof the ethos checker
accepted, cvc5 behind spec/smt-checked (ADR-0046 E2,
A1). Properties restated as Rust tests with the same
mutations, and every tested behaviour replayed through
spec/Mechanism.tla: 82 traces, 1,007 steps, every one
matching, each state read against the confinement
invariants (ADR-0033 A14)

text.tspan: What the reference does not claim

svg.text: Mutations and witnesses checked at small constants;
invariants proved of the modules, not of the code
A certified proof is not a verified one: the prover's
translation, its normalization, LS4 and the checker are
trusted. Three modules do not certify:
RulesFloorNV_rev5, Confinement, Confinement_A1
A matching trace is drift detection, not a refinement
(T-0045-28 stays a trust root).

text.tspan: Policy as code: a verified floor

svg.text: Floor tier: an evaluator with a mechanized semantics, an
implementation checked against it, and a decidable
comparison of two policy sets. Bundle tier: per-request,
signed, subtract-only.
Floor: Cedar (cedar-policy, the Rust engine) linked into
the replica, the gated floor compiled in by path and refused
unless its digests match: since 2026.10.05 the proposed
floor's emergency stage (
floor/proposed/emergency-floor.cedar, 28 policies,
107 cases), not the genesis draft (G10 §2.2; ADR-0033
A10–A12). Bundle: OPA/Rego sidecar with an in-process
WASM fallback bound to the lease's revision, loading only
a bundle signed under an issued key (ADR-0044) whose
allowlist is well-formed (ADR-0049)

text.tspan: What the reference does not claim

svg.text: Rego has no mechanized semantics, so it cannot hold
the floor tier (D-0030-1 if it does).
admit ⟺ floor_permit ∧ ¬bundle_deny (ADR-0030
No floor is ratified: the bootstrap reviewer establishes
fitness, and nothing written says what fit means (G10 §8;
item 87).
Order every grant and every authority fact in one log; the
log index is the fence. Consensus for grants, local for
denials.
Sans-IO crash-recovery Multi-Paxos (topak-paxos): a
Voting ghost under message-level Paxos, driven by a
deterministic simulation that checks Voting's invariants on
every durable vote.

text.tspan: What the reference does not claim

svg.text: Replicas are crash-recovery, not Byzantine (ADR-0033
Replica set is trust-root row T-0045-1; mutual
authentication between replicas is unbuilt (ADR-0045
Annex B).
Every agent is Byzantine at every position. It reaches the
world only through a typed alphabet; models stay out of
the trusted computing base.
The alphabet as MCP tools and nothing else, on a front
door the mechanism owns (topak mcp, stdio, bearer
token); downstream tools reached as MCP servers. A
guest the node launches is bridged on stdio and mints no
token (ADR-0033 A7). In Run every item delivered carries
a label, clear or as a handle, and the round opens with the
tool list (ADR-0047, ADR-0048; A10). Operators send
signed requests the floor's C1–C9 decide (ADR-0050; A11);
an emergency seat is activated by the roster's quorum
and signs each action (ADR-0052; A12)

text.tspan: What the reference does not claim

svg.text: The alphabet is the whole protocol, not the whole
channel: a process with a shell never has to ask.
Leases at rung 0, rung 1 on profiles that declare P3 fail
, rung 3 only SIMULATED: every real principal is
Mediated; an operator and an emergency seat by
design (G10 §2.3).
BOOTSTRAP: the unsigned operator socket seats and
does nothing else; a first lease from a quorum is not
built (G10 §8; item 88).
A label is one replica's computation, a declaration and
not a finding (G10 §8; item 93).
Transport with a durability window. Neither the ordering
authority (that is the Paxos log) nor the system of record
(that is the archive).
Kafka via rskafka (acks=all), one single-partition topic
per principal per round, opening with the tool list
(ADR-0042 A1); emissions after commit, denials
unordered, an after companion past the seal.

text.tspan: What the reference does not claim

svg.text: The K row rests on ADR-0005, ratified in Batch 27: the
debt ADR-0033 §2 carried since Batch 7 is discharged;
author-ratified until confirmed (C4).
Archive and erasure: not built.
Any row may change without amending the record, provided the replacement meets the role's obligation and the change is recorded in the reference's
assumptions register.
The floor row cannot change language without ADR-0030: Cedar meets the floor obligation; Rego does not.
Nothing translates: a Rego→Cedar transpiler would be a Build artifact whose output becomes the enforced floor.

text.tspan: The reference is evidence, not the verified object

svg.text: mechanism/ implements the admit path end to end for Build's six actions and Run's three (ADR-0033 §1), an operator's six control requests and an emergency
seating; rebuilt in five stages on 2026.10.05, 133 tests across thirteen binaries and 38 Rego tests (ADR-0033 A9–A15; G10 §3).
It has never been promoted, nothing in it is in any TCB, and it is not a deployment: it fails assumption of use A1.
It is cited like a TLA+ check: by manifest digest and commit, with the claim scoped to what its tests check.
§2.3, §2.9, §3, §8, §7 items 87, 88, 93; mechanism/README.md; README.md
